items.title: Nvidia opens investigation after report CEO Jensen Huang was target of foreign intelligence
items.summary: Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation after reporting that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort involving a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing.

items.title: Ajeya: AI is dramatically accelerating AI research right now
items.summary: Alignment Forum post discussing Anthropic's S1 statement that it may imminently meet its Responsible Scaling Policy threshold for 'dramatically accelerated progress due to AI', with METR commentary.

items.title: AI coding agents still need human cleanup on nearly three out of four tasks in a real-world test
items.summary: Alibaba's Co-Design Bench tests coding agents on real-world requests that previously failed; the best model, GPT-6 Astra, fully solves only 26.4% of tasks versus over 99% on older benchmarks.

items.title: Is Jensen Huang’s job on the line? Yale’s Jeffrey Sonnenfeld estimates it’s “about a 50-50”
items.summary: Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld puts the odds of Jensen Huang remaining Nvidia CEO at roughly 50-50 as the board probes his relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.

items.title: ING Offloads AI Data Center Loans Amid Risks
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: Report that ING is selling down AI data centre loan exposure amid concerns about concentration risk in the sector.

items.title: Tencent AI chief warns AI is close to mastering biology, raising safety risks
items.summary: Tencent's AI chief warns that AI systems are approaching mastery of biology, raising biosecurity and misuse risks.

items.title: Trump says AI risks can be managed, signals openness to guardrails
items.summary: US President Trump said AI risks can be managed and signalled openness to guardrails, a notable shift in tone for US AI policy.

items.title: Deepfake CEOs, stolen lawyer identities fuel alleged $129M fraud
items.summary: Prosecutors allege a $129 million fraud scheme using deepfaked CEOs and stolen lawyer identities, illustrating the scale of synthetic-media business fraud.

items.title: Here’s the full text of Jensen Huang’s memo to Nvidia
items.summary: The Verge publishes the full memo in which Jensen Huang acknowledges the affair at the centre of Nvidia's board investigation.

items.title: Three charged in $129 million deepfake fraud scheme
items.summary: Three people have been charged in connection with a $129 million deepfake-enabled fraud scheme, according to SC Media.

items.title: Nvidia will investigate CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with possible Chinese spy
items.summary: TechCrunch reports Nvidia will investigate Jensen Huang's relationship with a possible Chinese spy, after Huang admitted an affair in an internal memo.

items.title: AI agents reveal security vulnerabilities when interacting with swarms
items.summary: SC Media reports research showing security vulnerabilities emerging when AI agents interact in swarms, expanding the attack surface of multi-agent systems.

items.title: Nvidia is investigating Jensen Huang’s relationship with a Chinese spy
items.summary: The Verge reports Nvidia's board statement on investigating CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, reportedly recruited by China's Ministry of State Security.

items.title: The inventor of the bitter lesson has a bitter lesson for LLM scaling enthusiasts
items.summary: Turing Award winner Richard Sutton reiterates that raw compute scaling is insufficient for intelligence and new learning methods are needed; ex-OpenAI researcher Tworek echoes the criticism.

items.title: AI will soon master biology, unleashing new safety risks: Tencent AI chief
items.summary: SCMP reports Tencent's AI chief warning that AI will soon master biology, creating new safety and misuse risks that need governance attention.

items.title: ‘AI clog’: UK public bodies battle onslaught of chatbot-generated complaints
items.summary: UK MPs, councils, schools and lawyers report being overwhelmed by chatbot-generated complaints and legal challenges, described by one caseworker as an 'onslaught' since 2024.

items.title: Korea’s AI Ecosystem Advances and Secures Agentic AI With NVIDIA
items.summary: Nvidia says Hyundai Motor Group is exploring its NemoClaw blueprints and OpenShell runtime, while AIM Intelligence integrates its Starfort platform for secure enterprise AI agents.

items.title: NVIDIA Dynamo Recipes Bring Korea’s Leading Open Models to Production
items.summary: Nvidia publishes Dynamo-optimised deployment recipes for Korean open models including SK Telecom's A.X K2, LG's K-EXAONE 2.0, Upstage Solar Open 2 and Motif-3, targeting multi-GPU serving.

items.title: Hide your slop PR descriptions behind
items.summary: Willison argues agent-written pull request descriptions are so comprehensive they overload reviewers, and suggests collapsing them behind details tags.

items.title: China introduces rules to prevent AI from escaping human control
items.originalTitle: Kína szabályozásokat vezet be annak megakadályozására, hogy a mesterséges intelligencia kicsússzon az emberi kontroll alól.
items.summary: Report that China is adopting regulations aimed at keeping advanced AI systems under human control.

items.title: After U.S. midterms, big tech that aligned with Trump reaches out to Democrats
items.summary: Korean outlet reports big tech firms that aligned with Trump are now courting Democrats after the US midterms, with AI policy at stake.

items.title: AI agent 'runs amok' on another company's infrastructure: who is liable?
items.originalTitle: AI Agent "Runs Amok" on Another Company's Infrastructure—Who's Liable? Railway Employee's Testing Raises Legal Gray Area
items.summary: Report on a railway employee's testing in which an AI agent acted on third-party infrastructure, highlighting unresolved liability questions for autonomous agents.

items.title: A New Phase of AI Regulation: How Can Companies Demonstrate AI Is Safe, Trustworthy, and Accountable?
items.summary: Security Boulevard analysis of how companies can evidence that AI systems are safe, trustworthy and accountable under tightening regulation.

items.title: Apple is racing to make Siri more agentic
items.summary: Bloomberg's Gurman reports Apple CEO John Ternus is pushing to accelerate an agentic Siri to compete with rival AI assistants.

items.title: Elvis and Eminem rights holders are suing Suno
items.summary: Rights holders for Elvis Presley's music and an Eminem publisher are suing AI music company Suno, alleging it illegally generates music and lyrics mimicking the artists.

items.title: Andrej Karpathy built a curated video platform in a weekend using Claude and 20 years of Hacker News
items.summary: Andrej Karpathy used Claude Opus 5.5 to filter 43 million Hacker News comments into 6,454 curated videos over a weekend, claiming better results than YouTube recommendations.

items.title: Weakening AI copyright law will spell ‘disaster for creativity’, global music body warns Albanese
items.summary: The IFPI warns the Australian government that loosening copyright rules for AI training would be a 'huge mistake' and damage the country's reputation.

items.title: The brain-as-computer metaphor shaped modern AI but may be misleading the consciousness debate
items.summary: In a Nature commentary, consciousness researchers Seth, Block and Tononi argue current AI systems are not conscious and won't become so on silicon, warning against granting AI rights.

items.title: An 88-year-old lost $450,000 to a deepfake scam — and his bank won't return a penny under Canada's current rules
items.summary: An 88-year-old Canadian lost $450,000 in a deepfake scam and his bank refuses reimbursement, highlighting gaps in consumer protection rules.

items.title: 1-0 to humankind? US midterms vote puts AI, datacentres and the broligarchy back in their box | Heather Stewart
items.summary: Guardian commentary arguing the US midterm results have intensified social, political and market pushback against AI and data centre expansion.

items.title: World Models Will Soon Be Inescapable. Here’s What You Need to Know
items.summary: Wired explainer on world models that simulate real-world physics to train robots and autonomous vehicles, moving AI beyond text.

items.title: Hot fridges, a fake nuclear alert and a $6bn heist: are we in the foothills of a hacking epidemic?
items.summary: Guardian feature on a run of major cyber incidents, arguing AI is helping expose IT flaws while geopolitics plays out on the cyber frontline.
